caption: The post-training process described in Appendix <ref> decreases hallucinations. One measure is that the problems in SimpleQA—which the model very rarely gets correct—are increasingly not attempted during the course of post-training. We believe the final result is better behavior, even though the simple-evals score for SimpleQA (the F1 score) actually gives our base model a higher score than our final model.
model_annotation: The bar chart, titled "SimpleQA performance over the course of post-training," illustrates the distribution of model responses to SimpleQA problems across four stages: Base, SFT, DPO Stage 1, and Final. Each stage is represented by a stacked bar, with the total percentage of responses summing to 100%. The legend indicates three categories: "Correct" (green), "Not Attempted" (dark blue), and "Incorrect" (light blue). The vertical axis represents the percentage of responses, ranging from 0% to 100%. In the Base stage, the model correctly answers only 3.2% of questions, does not attempt 6.8%, and answers incorrectly 90.0%. As post-training progresses, the proportion of "Not Attempted" responses increases significantly, reaching 79.8% in DPO Stage 1 and 81.1% in the Final stage. The proportion of "Correct" responses remains low throughout, increasing slightly to 3.0% in the Final stage. The proportion of "Incorrect" responses decreases from 90.0% in the Base stage to 15.8% in the Final stage. The chart visually supports the caption's claim that the model increasingly refrains from attempting problems, particularly as hallucinations are reduced during post-training.
